description: Control systems design decomposed. PID tuning methods, root locus design, Bode design, state space (LQR, Kalman), observers, MIMO control, MPC formulation, anti-windup, gain scheduling.

sub_mechanisms.name: Ziegler_Nichols_tuning
sub_mechanisms.definition: Increase Kp until oscillation; record critical Kc + period Pc. Compute Kp, Ki, Kd from formulas.
sub_mechanisms.why: Classic empirical tuning. Aggressive response, often overshoot. Starting point; manual refinement common.

sub_mechanisms.name: Cohen_Coon_tuning
sub_mechanisms.definition: Open-loop step response: K, τ, θ. Compute PID gains.
sub_mechanisms.why: Better than Z-N for processes with significant dead time. Process industry default.

sub_mechanisms.name: lambda_tuning
sub_mechanisms.definition: λ = desired closed-loop time constant. Compute Kp from process model.
sub_mechanisms.why: Industrial tuning: target response speed. Conservative + robust. Standard in chemical processes.

sub_mechanisms.name: integrator_windup
sub_mechanisms.definition: Saturation: actuator at limit, integrator keeps accumulating. Recovery is sluggish.
sub_mechanisms.why: Common bug. Mitigations: anti-windup (clamp integrator at limit, back-calculation). Standard PID implementation feature.

sub_mechanisms.name: gain_scheduling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Different PID gains for different operating regions. Smooth interpolation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Process gains change with operating point. Aircraft: different gains at different speeds. Better than single tuning for wide-range systems.

sub_mechanisms.name: phase_margin_gain_margin
sub_mechanisms.definition: PM: phase between -180° at gain crossover. GM: gain below 1 at phase crossover.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stability margins. PM > 45°, GM > 6 dB standard. Read from Bode. Foundation of frequency-domain stability.

sub_mechanisms.name: loop_shaping_Bode
sub_mechanisms.definition: Design controller to shape open-loop frequency response: high gain low-freq, attenuation high-freq.
sub_mechanisms.why: Classical frequency-domain design. Lead, lag, lead-lag compensators. Standard control technique.

sub_mechanisms.name: state_observer_Luenberger
sub_mechanisms.definition: Estimate state from measurements. x̂' = Ax̂ + Bu + L(y - Cx̂).
sub_mechanisms.why: Most states not measured. Observer reconstructs. Combined with state feedback = full state control. Standard modern control.

sub_mechanisms.name: Kalman_filter_optimal_observer
sub_mechanisms.definition: Stochastic observer. Optimal state estimation under Gaussian noise.
sub_mechanisms.why: Already in embedded; here in control context. LQG = LQR + Kalman = optimal control + estimation. Standard for noisy systems.

sub_mechanisms.name: LQR_optimal_control
sub_mechanisms.definition: Linear Quadratic Regulator. Minimise ∫(x'Qx + u'Ru)dt. Solve Riccati equation for gain.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tradeoff Q (state penalty) vs R (control penalty). Modern multi-variable control. Standard for MIMO.

sub_mechanisms.name: MPC_formulation
sub_mechanisms.definition: At each time step: solve constrained optimisation over horizon; apply first control. Repeat.
sub_mechanisms.why: Handles constraints + multi-variable + nonlinearity. Drones, chemical processes. Computational cost = horizon × MIMO size.

sub_mechanisms.name: controllability_observability_tests
sub_mechanisms.definition: Controllability matrix rank n: can drive state anywhere. Observability matrix rank n: can reconstruct state from output.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundational state space property. Uncontrollable modes can't be controlled. Unobservable modes can't be estimated. Standard test.

derivation_rules.name: phase_margin_predicts_overshoot
derivation_rules.why: Rules of thumb: PM=45° → ~25% overshoot, PM=60° → ~10%. Phase margin is robustness against phase errors. Standard design target.

derivation_rules.name: anti_windup_essential_for_saturating_actuators
derivation_rules.why: Without: integrator keeps accumulating; recovery sluggish. With: clamp or back-calculate. Modern PID always includes. Standard practice.

derivation_rules.name: LQR_balances_state_control_effort
then: aggressive control, fast response, large effort
derivation_rules.why: Q penalises state deviation; R penalises control. Ratio determines tradeoff. Bryson's rule: Q_ii = 1/(max acceptable x_i)². Standard scaling.

derivation_rules.name: MPC_solves_constrained_optimisation_real_time
then: MPC enforces them at each step
derivation_rules.why: Classical PID + saturation: ad hoc. MPC: constraints explicit in optimisation. Cost: solve every sample. Used where constraints critical.

derivation_rules.name: controllability_test_before_design
derivation_rules.why: Uncontrollable system can't be moved anywhere. Wasted effort to design feedback. Standard verification before LQR / pole placement.
